subjects.introduction: Hospitals in Damascus with pharmacies and physicians, endowments for orphans, for strangers, even for servants who broke a dish and feared their master: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalls these to ask what became of a community whose first standard-bearers astonished the world. Bahá’u’lláh’s answer is unsparing and at moments grieving: as hearts darkened, justice was veiled and tyranny took its seat, power turned into weakness and courage into fear, and division did what no outside enemy could. The sharper charge concerns expectation. A people who waited twelve centuries for the Promised One, and counted as infidels any who said he would be born, found their books and anticipation turned into swords when the Báb appeared in Fars; inherited tales became veils thicker than the ones they replaced. None of this rests safely in the past, since the same warnings are turned on the followers of the Bayan and then on the Bahá’ís themselves. The Qur’an’s call to hold fast together and remember how former enemies became brothers offers a measure for any community. From here the road runs through Muhammad and the foundation of Islam, the wider story of corruption and renewal, and violence in the name of God, toward the plain work of justice, education and repair.
subjects.arc: Begin with Islam’s spiritual foundation and the costs of division, examine the sources’ accounts of authority, expectation, and persecution, then follow their warnings inward toward self-examination, education, justice, and renewal.

order.why: Read the letter’s account of early spiritual vitality and subsequent loss.
Place justice and equity at the center of the inquiry.
shortened: Iran is still in in a ruinous state, and until justice and equity become its foundation and basis, conditions will worsen day by day.

order.why: Open with the reported distinction between Islam’s foundation and what is commonly said about it.
Introduce division as the stated cause of weakness.
Hear grief over lost standing and the harm inflicted by the strong on the weak.
shortened: O thou who art remembered in the heart of this servant! The station of Islam hath declined, religion hath weakened, and the banners have been reversed. We must supplicate God at all times, at eventide and dawn, that He may assist His loved ones and servants and raise up one who shall arise to redress what hath been lost. Your honor hath heard what the strong hath wrought upon the weak, and what hath befallen God's cities and lands from cannons and rifles.

order.why: Ask with the source what causes decline and how knowing its cause might permit repair.
shortened: Surely you have heard the account of Alexandria and Islam and others. The divine religion hath been weakened and the adversary strengthened, yet the cause and reason for this weakness which hath persisted over successive years remaineth unknown and hidden from all. For were they to become aware of its cause and reason, they would surely arise to remove it.

order.why: Read sorrow over weakness as grief for a once powerful community.
shortened: These are days wherein a thousand sorrows appear at every moment, all being the results of deeds and actions. Matters have reached such a pass that the Islamic nation, which was the most powerful, greatest, most perfect and most rightful of all nations, has manifested such weakness that every person of conscience, every person of fairness, and every person of heart lamenteth over it. Verily, sighs ascend and tears descend, but most of the people are in evident delusion.

order.why: Consider the image of the religious body losing its members.
Hear the prayer to restore lost glory and strength.
shortened: Now we beseech and implore God, exalted be His glory, to adorn the lost glory with the ornament of existence, and to make manifest the vanished might before all faces. What happened to that power and strength, and what caused this weakness? Until now, all remain heedless of the cause and reason.

order.why: Keep the brief hope for rebuilding what was lost, with its omission.
Read the stated movement from justice toward tyranny.
shortened: In every moment, God's favor would arrive and victory would be granted, until hearts changed and grew dark. Gradually justice became veiled and tyranny appeared and became established in its place. Fairness was concealed behind clouds and oppression became manifest and evident in its stead. These matters became the cause and reason for the supreme abasement, as was and is witnessed: "The banners of misbelief flutter above the banners of unity."

order.why: Keep the remembered words about early striving and later weakness in their attribution.
Hear the concise contrast between former glory and present condition.
Read branching paths and weakened unity in the ocean image.
Keep the reported account of early effects followed by disputes.
Read the recollected statement about a good religion harmed by differences.
Consider the reported appeal to change as a feature of contingent existence.
Widen the inquiry through the source’s example from Christianity.
Read the concern about material causes becoming detached from their sustaining source.
Consider the gap between good intentions and effective action.
Keep the report of hospitals, schools, and endowments attributed as historical recollection.
shortened: In Damascus there was a great and well-organized hospital with a pharmacy and physicians. Nur al-Din Zangi, the Seljuk ruler, had established it in Damascus. He also established an asylum for the mentally ill. Now all of it is in ruins, and its endowments have been taken away.
This Islamic nation that was once at such heights--what has become of it now that they must beseech the Christians to admit them to their hospitals?
When one examines the histories of the Holy Manifestations of God, one sees what souls appeared, but when they turned away from God's Law, to what state they fell.

order.why: Read the criticism of education narrowed to disputes about words.
Consider the reported insistence that chastity must not prevent women’s learning.
Keep the concise reported criticism of a reduced understanding of justice.
Read the reported loss of fasting’s spiritual purpose.
Consider the reported disregard for listening during recitation.
shortened: Mohamadans having forgotten their reverence for the Holy things and overlooking the injunction of Mohamad smoke and talk on such occasions.

order.why: Read the critique of treating a verbal creed as sufficient for salvation.
Keep the report’s claims about fate, care, and children attributed to its source.
shortened: However, the Muslims do not follow the laws of the Qur'an and are unaware that it states fate is of two kinds, certain and alterable.
But a Muslim has twenty offspring and as he is careless in their affairs, they all roam the streets, expire and die.

order.why: Read the reported image of Rumi’s work buttressing a tilting wall.
Consider the report’s account of families moving from opposition to religious authority.
Read the reported interpretation of the companionship of Abu Bakr.
Keep the Tablet’s critique of contested authority and multiplying traditions in its polemical setting.
shortened: One reported Muhammad to have said "Were there to be a Prophet after Me, it would assuredly be 'Umar,"  and another related the hadith of "The ten promised the paradise."   One recited "'Uthman is the man of two lights"  and "'Uthman shall be my companion in the highest heaven,"  and another recounted Muhammad as having said "Were I to take any friend besides God, I would take Abu-Bakr."
In sum, the divines multiplied and their decrees proliferated.  The obscuring dust of lies and absurdities rose to heaven and the sun of truthfulness was wholly beclouded.

order.why: Read the reported criticism of traditions through their divisive consequences.
Consider the account of accusations made against Muhammad’s revelation.
Read the general warning about ignorance dressed as learning and wrongdoing as piety.
Keep the letter’s account of carefully reading a history of sectarian differences.
Read the described divisions after Hasan Askari as this letter’s historical account.
Keep the reported description of occultation beliefs explicitly attributed.
Hear the questions about expected signs in the Traveller’s Narrative.
shortened: What shall we make of the flight of the Guardians and the Helpers? How shall we deal with the conquest of the East and the West? Where is the Ass of Antichrist? When will the appearance of the Sufyan be? Where are the signs which are in the traditions of the Holy Family? Where is that whereon the Victorious Church is agreed?

order.why: Consider the reported test of accepting an unexpected command from the Qaim.
Read the Iqan’s argument that revelation is not bound to prior expectations.
shortened: It is the veil of idle imaginations which, in the days of the Manifestations of the Unity of God and the Daysprings of His everlasting glory, hath intervened, and will continue to intervene, between them and the rest of mankind. For in those days, He Who is the Eternal Truth manifesteth Himself in conformity with that which He Himself hath purposed, and not according to the desires and expectations of men. Even as He hath revealed: “So oft, then, as an Apostle cometh to you with that which your souls desire not, do ye swell with pride, and treat some as impostors, and slay others.”

order.why: Consider the Bab’s contrast between observance for God and failure to recognize the speaking Tree.
Read the claim that understanding Muhammad’s station would prepare recognition.
Keep the explanation of divine unity and the unknowable Essence central to the theological argument.
shortened: True belief in the unity of God [tawhid-i-haqiqi] consists in acknowledging and confessing the unity of God, exalted be His glory, sanctifying His Essence from all likeness and purifying His Being from all similitudes. This has ever been and shall ever be the case. The Shi'ih sect, however, failed to attain this most exalted station, this most glorious rank, this ultimate purpose and this most resplendent summit. For it is evident and proven to those immersed in the ocean of truth and them who hold fast to the cords of knowledge and wisdom that God, exalted be His glory, has ever been and shall ever be the Unknowable, the Inaccessible.

order.why: Read the accusation of forsaking the root for a branch.
Consider names becoming a barrier to their Owner in the source’s criticism.
Read the related criticism of attachment to names and competing leaders.
shortened: For ages and centuries the Shi'ih sect hath been occupied with the mention of names while remaining heedless and veiled from their Creator and Lord. Each day they cling to a deceiver and grasp the hem of one who sows doubt, warring amongst themselves.

order.why: Keep the brief description of boasting about succession.
shortened: O Hasan! For one thousand two hundred years the Shi'ih sect boasted from pulpits of Ali's successorship and recounted the virtues of the Imams.

order.why: Consider the question about the fruits of affirming succession.
Read the question about benefits actually derived from professed claims.
Hear the repeated appeal to take warning from the fruits of conduct.
Keep the summons to examine words and deeds.
Read the source’s test of vainglory through the balance of justice.
shortened: Consider the vainglory of the Shi'ih sect: they deemed themselves the foremost of the world and the most exalted among nations. Yet when the balance of justice was set up, they were found to be the most lost among the peoples of the world. They spent their entire lives occupied with successor-games and likewise with other names such as Chiefs and Nobles and the like.

order.why: Consider claims of others’ impurity beside the source’s account of persecution.
shortened: Reflect upon the Shi'ih sect and the pride and arrogance of those people. They regarded as unclean the Jews and Christians, and likewise the idol-worshippers and fire-worshippers. The People of the Sunna they deemed lower, more rejected and more abominable than all other sects. Yet on the Promised Day, with but a slight test, they were found to be the most lost of all upon the earth.

order.why: Keep the severe judgment about a failed test attributed to the letter.
shortened: The Shi'ih sect counted themselves the most learned, most excellent and most God-fearing among the world's peoples, yet with one clear test it became evident they were the basest of all the earth's peoples. They committed that which no other people in the world had committed.

order.why: Read the concise reversal of claimed superiority as polemical argument.
shortened: Glory be to God! The Shi'ih sect counted themselves the most excellent of all people, yet they were witnessed to be the most lost.

order.why: Keep the similar judgment in its own source.
Read the forceful claim of continuing heedlessness as the speaker’s judgment.
Keep the severe description beside the question of professed unity.
Read the declaration concerning idolatry as a source’s theological judgment.
shortened: By God's life! The Shi'ih sect hath been recorded in the Crimson Book by the Most Exalted Pen as being among the idolaters.

order.why: Preserve the source’s harsh comparisons without turning them into an editorial description of people.
shortened: All factions among the peoples have attained unto lofty stations, save the odious Shi'ih faction. Each day, like unto Pharaoh, they sink one or two spans deeper, and perceive it not.

They consider themselves the most exalted people in the world, and likewise the most learned, the most excellent and the most high, whereas in the estimation of those possessed of insight they were and are not even mentioned, and in the sight of the Concourse on High they are regarded as lower than animals.

order.why: Keep the reported prayer concerning another such sect explicitly attributed.
Read the prayer and criticism of confusing God with creation in its historical polemic.
Consider the prayer for protection from inherited fancies.
Keep the brief severe judgment in its own source setting.
shortened: Vain imaginings deprived the Shi'ih sect from the Lord of mankind and consigned them to hell.

order.why: Read inherited tales as the named veil.
Consider the account of replacing one veil with another and the plea for independent courage.
shortened: O true brother and real beloved! One cannot speak the truth, as in most instances flows from the Pen of the All-Merciful: "Whatever thick veils and massive coverings We rent asunder by the finger of power, yet it was observed that the people had fashioned for themselves veils thicker than those and coverings greater than those." For a thousand years and more, imaginary creatures who deemed themselves the gems of existence were gazing toward and turned to an imaginary city, an unknown cellar, and a precinct of fancy. And from time to time mention was made of communications that would emerge from that precinct. O God! Is there any one strong whom the fancies of men cannot weaken, and any one assured whom the clamor of the servants cannot frighten?

order.why: Keep the claim concerning imaginary cities and an awaited figure attributed.
Read the accusation of manipulating people through supposed secrets.
Consider the letter’s account of tales establishing authority.
Read the questions about Jabulqa and the defense of Jafar.
Keep the companion statement concerning Jafar in its own form.
shortened: For one thousand two hundred years they called the son of the Imam a liar by their own admission and he became known as Ja'far the Liar, while that helpless one spoke but one word in truth.

order.why: Consider the stated consequence of interpreting words through desire and enforcing beliefs by threat.
shortened: For most of the servants have been and continue to be vessels of ignorance and corruption, ever waiting to invalidate truth or to clothe falsehood in the garment of truth. Even as the divines of Iran from the inception of Islam until now maintain that the Promised One dwells in Jabulqa and Jabulsa, and whosoever speaks otherwise, they pronounce his death sentence and mock the Sunnis, since those souls do not cling to such invented fancies but rather affirm and proclaim His birth.

order.why: Keep the source’s argument about the Bab’s birth and inherited expectations attributed.
shortened: The Shi'ih sect, who counted themselves as the saved and blessed community and knew themselves as the most excellent of all people, related successive traditions stating that whosoever claimed the Promised One would be born was an infidel and outside the religion. These traditions caused many to be martyred without guilt or crime, until the Primal Point - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him - was born in Fars from the loins of a known person and made the claim of being the Qa'im.

order.why: Read the accusation concerning divines and the denial of Jabulqa.
Keep the claim linking education in fancies to a death warrant.
Read the accusation that religious education prevented recognition.
shortened: The cause and reason for this heedlessness and ignorance were and are the Shi'ih divines, who have educated people in vain imaginings and idle fancies until at last they were deprived of the ocean of manifestation and the call of the Speaker on Sinai.

order.why: Consider the roles attributed to suspicion and calumny.
Keep the categorical claim about the divines’ failure attributed to this source.
Criticizes religious learning that becomes a barrier to recognition and a source of harm.
Read the address to a handmaiden concerning deprivation through fancies.
Consider the counsel to a seeker about detachment from inherited arguments.
shortened: The first thing that is incumbent upon the sincere seeker is sanctification and detachment from the tales, proofs and arguments to which the Shi'ih party hath clung. By God! They are in manifest error. Their remembrances are but calumnies. Heedlessness hath reached such a point that they curse from their pulpits the Manifestations of God's attributes and names, and they perceive it not.

order.why: Read the warning about following desire and fabricated claims.
Keep the severe warning concerning recitation accompanied by denial.
Read the connection drawn between competing claims and recurring strife.
Consider mutual denunciation, death decrees, and the construction of authority.
shortened: For one thousand two hundred years the misguided and misleading sect - namely the Shi'ih - both learned and ignorant among them, have occupied themselves with mention of guardian, successor, Imam, chief and noble, and such like, and such was the intensity of the hatred and animosity between their factions that each party would denounce the other as infidel and decree their death, while through the architects of suspicion and fancy they built up dominions.

order.why: Keep the image of factions praising their own learning while cursing one another.
Read disputes among named factions followed by the decisive test.
Keep the source’s emphatic description of hatred attributed.
Hear the pulpit lamenting its use for cursing.
Read expectation of divine presence followed by reviling.
Consider the contrast between seeking by night and day and rejecting the One sought.
Keep the account of invocations of the Qaim followed by violent opposition.
Read the growing Tree confronted by swords.
Hear the cities of justice lamenting the reported response.
Read the account of the awaited dawn and violence against the Tree.
Keep denial, objection, and judgment to shed blood as distinct responses.
Read the lament over slaying the One long awaited.
Consider the source’s extended account of curses and the shedding of blood.
Keep the concise statement concerning the Bab’s martyrdom.
Read the brief comparative condemnation as the source’s assertion.
shortened: The Shi'ih sect committed that which no other sect hath ever committed.

order.why: Keep the account of verdicts, plunder, and death within its historical denunciation.
Read the contrast between persecution and receptive people in named regions.
Consider mourning Husayn while reviling revelation as the letter’s charge of contradiction.
shortened: The corruption of this sect is more evident than the sun in the midst of heaven. In the early days, all were occupied with cursing, denouncing and rejection. The heedlessness of these souls reached such a degree that they would mention the Prince of Martyrs from the pulpits and weep, and then curse and denounce the One by Whose word a thousand Husayns sacrificed their lives in the field of martyrdom, and from the pulpit they would hasten towards hell.

order.why: Keep the contradiction between grieving Husayn and harming his children explicit.
shortened: They claim to have faith yet deny Him Who did ordain and send it forth, and they weep for Husayn while they slay his children.

order.why: Read the account of persecution and alleged newspaper calumnies with its qualifications.
shortened: The divines of the Shi'ih sect cried out "O Truth!" for years and awaited His appearance, yet when the morn of God's Day dawned and wondrous fruits appeared from the Blessed Tree, all attacked with sword and arrow. Now from all pulpits they revile the Truth, exalted be His glory.

order.why: Keep the strong claims about divines and death warrants attributed.
shortened: The word spoken aforetime hath been fulfilled: "Most of His enemies shall be the divines." The pride of that party was that they believed in the immediate successor, yet they openly reviled and issued death warrants against Him through Whose word a thousand successors and guardians were created. They have committed that which neither Jews, nor Christians, nor Zoroastrians committed.

order.why: Hear the despair and judgment arising from the source’s account of persecution.
Read verbal confession beside the accusation of tyranny.
Keep the prayer for unity alongside the source’s omission and condemnation.
Read books and expectation becoming swords in the letter’s image.
shortened: Observe the deeds of the people of the Furqan, that thou mayest become aware and informed of what was wrought against the All-Merciful. For twelve hundred years or more they were occupied with discourse and study, in the nights and days they clung to the reading of books, beseeching and hoping from God, exalted be His glory, for the days of His manifestation. Yet when the Day-Star of the Cause dawned from the horizon of the Divine Will, all that anticipation and all those books and readings appeared as swords, and there befell the Beloved of the worlds that which caused the rocks to cry out and the clouds to wail....

order.why: Preserve the selected accusation concerning doctrine and death rulings without supplying its antecedent.
Keep the criticism of worship divorced from knowledge in its polemical wording.
Consider the accusation that spoken thirst lacks a corresponding response.
Read the call from Hijaz through Shiraz and the Blessed Spot as the source’s account of revelation.
Keep the report’s contrast of beliefs about meeting God in its own terms.
Read the concise reported criticism of disregarded knowledge and power.
Consider the letter’s concern about power and oppression.
shortened: O beloved of my heart! The heedlessness and pride of the people of the world have deprived them of that which profits them. They were disturbed and distressed by the might of Islam and the power of its kings, and now matters have reached such a pass that every misbeliever has arisen to perpetrate oppression and has brought about whatever he desired.

order.why: Read the account of outside powers and its moral interpretation.
shortened: The Dove of Utterance hath cooed upon the twigs of mystic knowledge: The Kingdom belongeth unto God, the Lord of all worlds. This is a word uttered by the tongue of the Lord of Names after the passing away of all things. He, verily, is the Omnipotent, the Almighty. This is a day wherein the powers have risen against the Islamic Faith, whereby the foundations have been shaken and the people are in manifest loss. They have reaped what they have sown in their vain life, to which every discerning sage doth testify.

order.why: Keep the image of a fallen standard and shattered throne.
Read the same image linked to broken Covenant and neglected teachings.
shortened: The standard of Islam hath been reversed and its throne demolished by what the hands of the heedless have wrought - they who broke God's Covenant and Testament and cast aside what was sent down from His mighty and wondrous Kingdom.

order.why: Keep the letter’s view of government and order within its historical context.
shortened: Gracious God! Persia is deteriorating day by day as a result of disarray, and now that His Majesty's government has on its own volition and with goodwill resolved to bring some order and direction to the affairs of the country, it behooveth the population and particularly the leaders of the community to express their utmost gratitude to the officials for this lofty impetus.

order.why: Read the account of rejected unity and political provocation with its omission.
Keep the criticism of the named Democratic Party’s circumstances historical.
Read the report of Arabs, British power, and competing claims in its postwar setting.
shortened: See how many disturbances there are now! England has come and has faced the Arabs from the Turkish force. For 600 years the Arabs have been enslaved, and now they are free, their children, their wives, and their property. Now that they are free they say to the English "What are doing here?" We do not want you. Get out of our country. England replied "I have spent my (life) here, much English blood has been shed, I have spent much money. Am I going to leave now? I have freed you from this slavery.

order.why: Keep the report’s criticism of declarations of jihad and bribery attributed.
shortened: Jihad had an effect at a time when people were devoted to God's Faith, but now that spirit is completely gone. They themselves do not believe what they say. They claim this issue is a global war and jihad must be a matter of national concern. If in truth these people believed in religion, by now the world would have become the Abha paradise. If you offer them a bribe, they would say the exact opposite of what they ruled earlier. No trace of spirit, sincerity, faith, certitude or firmness has remained in Islam. Only mere words have survived."

order.why: Read the reported explanations of weakened zeal as interpretations of that moment.
shortened: In these days, the law of Jihad is shorn of much of its spiritual power, because the Mohamadans have become more intelligent and are not easily swept away by a seeming torrent of prejudices. Some, however, think that the Mohamadan world is divested of much of its former Faith and Zeal on account of clerical innovations.

order.why: Consider the reported criticism of violence, imitation, and political methods.
Read the related rejection of militancy as a sufficient means of religious advance.
Keep the broad reported judgment concerning spiritual and political power in its historical setting.
Read the brief reported pilgrimage practice without adding a missing narrative.
shortened: To the travelers, even today is pointed out this historical well and it is the religious duty of each Pilgrim going to Mecca annually to throw on that exact spot five stones which by this time it has become almost a hill.

order.why: Turn the warning inward toward those repeating earlier conduct.
Read the explicit application of the criticism to followers of the Bayan.
Consider the call to guide others while recognizing repeated patterns of denial.
shortened: Consider the Shi'ih sect. For years they considered themselves the best of creation, yet with the slightest test it became evident they were the basest of servants, as evidenced by their martyrdom of the Bab. Now too the deniers among the Bayan cling to the same vain imaginings. Whatever fruit the Shi'ih sect reaped from the tree of their deeds, these souls shall reap as well. You must, with the utmost joy and fragrance, remind the people and guide them to the highest horizon.

order.why: Keep the warning about reviving former patterns within its severe language.
Read the claim that the same names and attitudes have reappeared.
Consider the warning about newly reviving the criticized pattern.
Read the specific appeal for followers of the Bayan to awaken.
Keep the source’s comparison involving true and false Ali in its polemical setting.
Read the reported encounter and laughter as an attributed episode.
Keep the allegations concerning a particular opponent within their source; do not generalize them.
shortened: After that supreme martyrdom which caused earth and heaven to weep, that faithless one occupied himself with women, holding feasts each day and entering bridal chambers. He wrote seven letters to seven martyrs, requesting from each a virgin, and when his purpose was not achieved, he grew bold and impudent, laying hands on the chaste Mother of the Believers, taking as wife the second consort of the Exalted One despite the explicit prohibition in the Book, and not satisfied with that, after a few days gave her to the rejected Siyyid Muhammad.

order.why: Consider the reported warning that divisive claims could arise among Bahais.
Read the warning about another cycle of authority and deception with its omission.
Hear the call for steadfastness and protection from deceptive authority.
Read the direct counsel to the people of God not to repeat the pattern.
Consider the fruits of conduct as a warning concerning the Covenant.
Keep the warning that a removed veil can be replaced by another.
shortened: The people are seen to be so heedless that one is astonished. If one veil is rent asunder, they are found to be afflicted with another veil greater than the first. For twelve hundred years and more, the well-known sect was occupied with calumny, slander and the like. At the time of the test, it became clear and evident to every person of insight that that rebellious and transgressing sect was the party of Satan, not the hosts of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Hear the summons to service alongside the source’s criticism of past conduct.
shortened: Arise, through the power and might of God, to serve the Cause. The world passeth away, but that which is with God endureth. From the beginning of Islam until this hour, not one among the divines hath been truly aware of the manner of His Revelation, and among the party of the Shi'ah there hath been naught but cursing and abuse.

order.why: Read the proclamation that veils have been rent and a new Day appeared.
Read the personal thanksgiving for a changed religious allegiance.
shortened: O Muhammad, praise be to the Lord of the worlds Who purified thee from the Shi'ih sect and what they possess with the water of the Bayan of His chosen ones, and guided thee to His Most Holy Court.

order.why: Keep the remembrance of those who chose what God loves.
Read the reported hope for cleansing and renewal attributed to its source.
Hear the hope of spiritual renewal in Iran with its omission.
Close the linked readings with the reported call to universal peace.
Read the supplied critique of superstition across religions and the appeal to knowledge.
shortened: All religions of the present day have fallen into superstitious practices, out of hamony alike with the true principles of the teaching they represent and with the scientific discoveries of the time. Many religious leaders have grown to think that the importance of religion lies mainly in the adherence to a collection of certain dogmas and the practice of rites and ceremonies! Those whose souls they profess to cure are taught to believe likewise, and these cling tenaciously to the outward forms, confusing them with the inward truth. Now, these forms and rituals differ in the various churches and amongst the different sects, and even contradict one another; giving rise to discord, hatred, and disunion.
But the religion which does not walk hand in hand with science is itself in the darkness of superstition and ignorance.

order.why: Consider the supplied hope for renewal of Christianity’s spiritual life.
End with the supplied counsel to build the future while sympathizing with those disoriented by change.
shortened: Even though the Baha'i Youth should feel with the condition in which they see their non-Baha'i friends and not indict them for it, they should not let themselves be carried by the wave of world events as they are being carried. Whereas they see before them only a world that is crumbling down we are also seeing a new world being built up. Whereas they experience the destruction of old institutions that commanded their respect, we are beholding the dawn of a new era with its strict commands and new social bonds. Their materialistic outlook shows them the futility of all things while our faith in a regenerated and spiritualized man makes us look to the future and build for it. To make them follow our ways we should sympathize with their plight but should not follow their ways. We should take our stand on a higher plane of moral and spiritual life and, setting for them the true example, urge them up to our level.

questions: What qualities do these sources associate with a religious community’s original vitality, and what do they identify as signs of decline?

How does the Qur’anic call to unity illuminate the contrast between professed faith and divisive conduct?
Why do several passages direct the warning toward the writers’ own followers, and what might that imply for any community’s self-examination?
What forms of education, justice, compassionate action, and peacebuilding might make renewal visible in communal life?
